extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations. It covers four task families—speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval—across 102 languages from more than 10 language families, and includes a new multilingual evaluation dataset called Fleurs.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S is assembled by grouping several existing multilingual speech datasets and by building a new dataset, Fleurs. For Fleurs, the authors use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the publicly available FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages, collect between one and three recordings for each sentence, and create new train-dev-test splits. For Minds-14, they merge monolingual datasets into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark uses existing datasets Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-14. Fleurs is built from 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, with collected speech recordings. MLS is derived from read audiobooks of LibriVox. VoxPopuli contains speech from European Parliament sessions. CoVoST-2 is a multilingual speech translation corpus. For the Fleurs retrieval task, transcription candidates are augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia, and the pool may combine additional sentences from Wikipedia or CommonCrawl.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs-ASR, the paper states: "We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages. We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average), and build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively."
extraction.rai:dataBiases: results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in Western European languages from MLS and VoxPopuli
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated; Test sets are available in open-source and are not hidden to the public, so users are asked to be careful not to inadvertently overfit on the test set; Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster; We hope XTREME-S will enable the community to build better speech representations in many languages, and enable rapid access to data-efficient speech technology for all the world’s languages
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages; simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation; catalyze research in universal speech representation learning; evaluate the generalization ability of multilingual speech pre-trained models
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For each language, the pool of transcription candidates is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: we provide scripts to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps
